title: Service Creation Followed By Execution Of The Same Binary
detection_hypothesis: If service-based persistence is established and used, a service installation record will be followed by a process creation record for the identical binary path on the same host.

field_semantics.Computer: Host on which the event was produced.
field_semantics.EventID: Numeric identifier of the Windows event record.
field_semantics.Image: Absolute path of the executable backing the created process.
field_semantics.ImagePath: Executable path configured for the service, including arguments.
field_semantics.Provider_Name: Name of the event provider that raised the record.

collection_prerequisites: A process creation source is enabled (Sysmon Event ID 1 or Security Event ID 4688).
Command-line auditing is enabled when Security 4688 is the only available source.
Service Control Manager events are not filtered out by the forwarder subscription.
The System event log is collected from endpoints and servers.
expected_collection_gaps: Security 4688 without command-line auditing provides no CommandLine value.
Servers with aggressive System log filters may drop Event ID 7045.
Service installation performed by driver loading is not represented here.
Short-lived processes may be lost if the agent is restarted during collection.
normalization_assumptions: CommandLine retains the original argument order and spacing.
Image and ParentImage are absolute paths using backslash separators.
ImagePath contains the full service binary path including any arguments.
ingestion_differences: Quoted service paths may or may not retain surrounding quotation marks.
Some pipelines lowercase paths; the lab matcher is case-insensitive by default.
Some pipelines rename ImagePath to service.executable.
Sysmon and 4688 differ in parent process fidelity and in User field formatting.
retention_considerations: Process creation is high volume; 30 to 90 days of hot retention is typical. System log volume is low; 365 days of retention is generally affordable.
expected_volume: Moderate before path filtering; low afterwards.
false_positive_strategy: Every managed agent installation produces this shape. The discriminator is the binary path, so combine this correlation with the user-writable service path rule and alert only on paths outside managed directories.
tuning_guidance: Filter the base service rule to user-writable image paths in noisy environments rather than raising the correlation timespan.
test_strategy: Positive sequences install and then execute the same path on one host. Negative sequences reverse the order, use different paths, and use different hosts.

attack_techniques.name: Create or Modify System Process: Windows Service
